title: Payback Periods & Revenue Modeling
description: Master CAC payback period calculations, revenue model comparisons, and LTV-to-CAC ratio analysis for real businesses.

interactions.prompt: If a SaaS company spends $600 to acquire a customer generating $50/month in gross profit, what is the CAC payback period?
interactions.teachingPreamble: CAC payback period measures how many months it takes to recoup your customer acquisition cost from gross profit. It's calculated as CAC ÷ monthly gross profit per customer. Investors typically want payback under 12-18 months for SaaS — Slack achieved ~11 months at scale.

interactions.prompt: A meal-kit company reports: CAC $120, ARPU $60/month, gross margin 33%, average customer lifespan 8 months. Monthly churn is 12.5%. What's the most critical red flag?

options.text: ARPU is too low for the category
CAC payback is 6 months but customers only last 8
Gross margin is healthy for meal-kits

interactions.prompt: A fitness app has LTV of $360 and CAC of $120. What is the LTV:CAC ratio, and how should the company interpret it?

options.text: 3:1 — over-investing, should spend more on growth

interactions.teachingPreamble: The LTV:CAC ratio is the north star of unit economics. A ratio of 3:1 is the widely-accepted benchmark — meaning you earn $3 for every $1 spent acquiring a customer. Below 1:1 you're losing money; above 5:1 you may be under-investing in growth. HubSpot targets 3:1 across its segments.

interactions.prompt: In a subscription model, LTV can be estimated as ARPU × Gross Margin ÷ ____, where the denominator represents the percentage of customers lost each period.

Your e-commerce startup has LTV:CAC of 2.5:1 and 14-month payback. You can either cut CAC 30% by dropping paid social (slower growth) or launch a loyalty program costing $15/user that extends average lifespan by 40%. Which do you choose?

options.text: Cut CAC — improves ratio and payback immediately
Launch loyalty program — higher LTV drives long-term value
Do both simultaneously to maximize impact
Do neither — focus on raising prices instead

interactions.prompt: A B2B SaaS company charges $200/month with 70% gross margin and 2% monthly churn. Estimate the gross-profit LTV per customer.
interactions.teachingPreamble: To estimate gross-profit LTV in subscription businesses, use: (ARPU × Gross Margin) ÷ Churn Rate. This gives you the total gross profit a customer generates over their lifetime. Sophisticated models discount future cash flows, but this quick formula — used widely in VC due diligence — gets you within striking distance.

interactions.prompt: A DTC skincare brand has a 22-month CAC payback period. Rank these interventions from most to least impactful on reducing payback period: (a) Increase prices 10%, (b) Reduce CAC by improving ad conversion rates, (c) Add a referral program, (d) Launch a subscription option to reduce churn.

options.text: Reduce CAC by improving ad conversion rates
Launch a subscription option to reduce churn

interactions.prompt: Your SaaS company just landed an enterprise deal: one client paying $50K/year with a 3-year contract, but onboarding cost $40K. Meanwhile your self-serve product has CAC of $200 and LTV of $900. Which channel deserves more investment?

options.text: Enterprise — higher absolute profit per deal

interactions.priorContext: Previously you analyzed a standard SaaS model with $200/month ARPU and 2% churn. Now the company has two distinct channels with vastly different unit economics — enterprise sales vs. self-serve — forcing you to compare across revenue models rather than optimize a single one.
